008642:     CIntegerIrLocal* local = c_ir_find_local_by_entity(builder, entity);
008643:     if (place.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !local)
008644:     {
008645:         return false;
008646:     }
008647:     local->is_parameter = true;
008648:     // The pointer an array parameter was adjusted to points at the element
008649:     // type, qualifiers included: `const struct timespec times[2]` yields a
008650:     // modifiable pointer to constant elements, so the read-only answer moves
008651:     // from the object to what it points to.
008652:     if (entity.value < builder->parse.entity_count)
008653:     {

008655:         if (declared.value < builder->parse.type_count && builder->parse.types[declared.value].kind == C_TYPE_ARRAY &&

008658:             builder->function->values[place.value].points_to_read_only = true;
008659:         }
008660:     }

008662:     u64* immediate = arena_allocate(builder->arena, u64, 1);
008663:     immediate[0] = argument_index;
008664:     IrSourceRange argument_source = c_ir_token_source_range(builder, name);
008665:     IrInstruction argument = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_ARGUMENT, type);
008666:     argument.immediates = immediate;
008667:     argument.immediate_count = 1;
008668:     argument.result = value;
008669:     IrInstructionId id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, argument, argument_source);
008670:     builder->function->values[value.value].definition = id;
008671:     bool stored = c_ir_emit_store(builder, local, value, argument_source);
008672:     if (stored)
008673:     {
008674:         c_ir_mark_local_read_only(builder, local);
008675:     }
008676:     return stored;
008677: }

008911: 
008912: // The imaginary suffix of a floating literal. C's suffixes are `f`/`l` and
008913: // GNU adds `i`/`j` for an imaginary constant, in either order and either
008914: // case, so the run of trailing letters is scanned rather than just the last
008915: // one. Reports the spelling with the imaginary letter removed, which is an
008916: // ordinary real literal the parser below already understands; `arena` is only
008917: // touched when that letter is not the last one.
008918: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_number_imaginary_spelling(Arena* arena, String8 spelling, String8* real_out)
008919: {
008920:     u64 suffix_start = spelling.length;
008921:     u64 imaginary_index = spelling.length;
008922:     while (suffix_start)
008923:     {
008924:         u8 byte = (u8)spelling.pointer[suffix_start - 1];
008925:         if (byte == 'i' || byte == 'I' || byte == 'j' || byte == 'J')
008926:         {
008927:             // Two imaginary letters is not a literal any compiler accepts;
008928:             // leave it alone and let the real parser refuse the spelling.
008929:             if (imaginary_index != spelling.length)
008930:             {
008931:                 return false;
008932:             }
008933:             imaginary_index = suffix_start - 1;
008934:         }
008935:         else if (byte != 'f' && byte != 'F' && byte != 'l' && byte != 'L')
008936:         {
008937:             break;
008938:         }
008939:         suffix_start -= 1;
008940:     }
008941:     if (imaginary_index == spelling.length || !suffix_start)
008942:     {
008943:         return false;
008944:     }
008945:     if (imaginary_index == spelling.length - 1)
008946:     {
008947:         *real_out = (String8){.pointer = spelling.pointer, .length = spelling.length - 1};
008948:         return true;
008949:     }
008950:     char8* copy = arena_allocate(arena, char8, spelling.length - 1);
008951:     memcpy(copy, spelling.pointer, imaginary_index);
008952:     memcpy(copy + imaginary_index, spelling.pointer + imaginary_index + 1, spelling.length - imaginary_index - 1);
008953:     *real_out = (String8){.pointer = copy, .length = spelling.length - 1};
008954:     return true;
008955: }
008956: 
008957: // The suffix of a floating constant: how many trailing bytes it occupies and
008958: // which type it names, reported as one code. C's suffixes are `f`/`F` for
008959: // float and `l`/`L` for long double, and C23 adds `f16`/`F16` for `_Float16`
008960: // -- the only one longer than a letter, so reading the last byte alone cannot
008961: // recognize it. The half suffix reports as 'h', a letter C does not use as a
008962: // suffix, so a caller comparing against 'f' or 'l' cannot confuse the two.
008963: // Every spelling-to-value path shares this so that the type a literal is
008964: // given and the digits that are parsed for it cannot disagree.
008965: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL u32 c_ir_float_suffix(String8 spelling, char8* code_out)
008966: {
008967:     // In a hexadecimal spelling `f` and `F` are digits, and only a `p`
008968:     // exponent makes such a spelling a floating constant at all: `0x2f16` is
008969:     // the integer 12054 and `0x2f` the integer 47, where `0x1p4f` really does
008970:     // carry the float suffix. Asking for the exponent is what keeps a
008971:     // float-typed initializer written with a hexadecimal integer from losing

015328: // Read the sign in the original format: a floating conversion can quiet a
015329: // signaling NaN or raise overflow/underflow, neither of which signbit permits.
015330: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_signbit_value(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CToken token, IrValueId value)
015331: {
015332:     IrValueId result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015333:     IrTypeId value_type = value.value < builder->function->value_count ? builder->function->values[value.value].canonical_type : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
015334:     IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, value_type);
015335:     if (type && type->kind == IR_TYPE_FLOAT && (type->bit_width == 32 || type->bit_width == 64 || type->bit_width == 80 || type->bit_width == 128))
015336:     {
015337:         IrSourceRange source = c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token);
015338:         u32 width = type->bit_width;
015339:         CTypeKind bits_kind = width == 32 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT : width == 80 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_SHORT : C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LONG_LONG;
015340:         IrTypeId bits_type = c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, bits_kind);
015341:         IrValueId slot = c_ir_emit_temporary(builder, value_type, source);
015342:         if (bits_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && slot.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID &&
015343:             c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, slot, value_type, value, source))
015344:         {
015345:             IrTypeId bits_pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, bits_type);
015346:             IrValueId address = c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, slot, value_type, source);
015347:             IrValueId bits_address = address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && bits_pointer_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
015348:                                          ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, bits_pointer_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015349:             IrValueId bits_place = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015350:             if (bits_address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015351:             {
015352:                 // The supported formats are little-endian. The wide sign field
015353:                 // starts at byte eight: the x87 sign/exponent or binary128 high limb.
015354:                 if (width > 64)
015355:                 {
015356:                     IrValueId index = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, width == 80 ? 4u : 1u, false, token, builder->s32_type);

015358:                     {

015360:                     }
015361:                 }
015362:                 else
015363:                 {
015364:                     bits_place = c_ir_emit_dereference_place(builder, bits_address, source);
015365:                 }
015366:             }
015367:             IrValueId bits = bits_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_load_place_raw(builder, bits_place, bits_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015368:             IrValueId shift = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, width == 32 ? 31u : width == 80 ? 15u : 63u, false, token, bits_type);
015369:             if (bits.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && shift.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015370:             {

015382: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_math_call(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CToken token, String8 link_name, IrValueId* arguments, u32 argument_count)
015383: {
015384:     // `__builtin_huge_val()` is a constant-valued compiler intrinsic.  Keep
015385:     // it in the math-builtin path so hosted headers can use the spelling
015386:     // without declaring a runtime symbol, but emit the IEEE positive
015387:     // infinity directly in canonical IR.
015388:     if (string_equal(link_name, S8("huge_val")))
015389:     {
015390:         if (argument_count != 0)
015391:         {
015392:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015393:         }
015394:         IrSourceRange source = c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token);
015395:         return c_ir_emit_builtin_float_bits(builder, builder->f64_type, UINT64_C(0x7ff0000000000000), source, S8("HUGE_VAL"));
015396:     }
015397:     // `__builtin_inff()` is the single-precision counterpart used by the
015398:     // hosted <math.h> INFINITY macro.  It is a constant-valued intrinsic, so
015399:     // do not require a runtime `inff` declaration or linker symbol.
015400:     if (string_equal(link_name, S8("inff")))
015401:     {
015402:         if (argument_count != 0)
015403:         {
015404:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015405:         }
015406:         IrSourceRange source = c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token);
015407:         return c_ir_emit_builtin_float_bits(builder, builder->f32_type, UINT64_C(0x7f800000), source, S8("INFF"));
015408:     }
015409:     // The builtin NaN constructors are compile-time values.  Do not create
015410:     // an imported `nan*` symbol: hosted headers use these names before a
015411:     // runtime library declaration exists, and the quiet IEEE payload is
015412:     // target-independent for the f32/f64 types represented by canonical IR.

015421:         if (!type || type->kind != IR_TYPE_FLOAT)
015422:         {
015423:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015424:         }

015427:                                                                                        : UINT64_C(0x7ff8000000000000),

015431:     {

015435:     bool isinf_builtin = string_equal(link_name, S8("isinf")) || string_equal(link_name, S8("isinff"));

015437:     bool isfinite_builtin = string_equal(link_name, S8("isfinite"));

015445:         {

015447:             // in binary64 against both signed infinities; NaN is unordered,

015328: // Read the sign in the original format: a floating conversion can quiet a
015329: // signaling NaN or raise overflow/underflow, neither of which signbit permits.
015330: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_signbit_value(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CToken token, IrValueId value)
015331: {
015332:     IrValueId result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015333:     IrTypeId value_type = value.value < builder->function->value_count ? builder->function->values[value.value].canonical_type : IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
015334:     IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, value_type);
015335:     if (type && type->kind == IR_TYPE_FLOAT && (type->bit_width == 32 || type->bit_width == 64 || type->bit_width == 80 || type->bit_width == 128))
015336:     {
015337:         IrSourceRange source = c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token);
015338:         u32 width = type->bit_width;
015339:         CTypeKind bits_kind = width == 32 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT : width == 80 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_SHORT : C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LONG_LONG;
015340:         IrTypeId bits_type = c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, bits_kind);
015341:         IrValueId slot = c_ir_emit_temporary(builder, value_type, source);
015342:         if (bits_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && slot.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID &&
015343:             c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, slot, value_type, value, source))
015344:         {
015345:             IrTypeId bits_pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, bits_type);
015346:             IrValueId address = c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, slot, value_type, source);
015347:             IrValueId bits_address = address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && bits_pointer_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
015348:                                          ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, bits_pointer_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015349:             IrValueId bits_place = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015350:             if (bits_address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015351:             {
015352:                 // The supported formats are little-endian. The wide sign field
015353:                 // starts at byte eight: the x87 sign/exponent or binary128 high limb.
015354:                 if (width > 64)
015355:                 {
015356:                     IrValueId index = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, width == 80 ? 4u : 1u, false, token, builder->s32_type);
015357:                     if (index.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015358:                     {
015359:                         bits_place = c_ir_emit_index_place(builder, bits_address, index, source);
015360:                     }
015361:                 }
015362:                 else
015363:                 {
015364:                     bits_place = c_ir_emit_dereference_place(builder, bits_address, source);
015365:                 }
015366:             }
015367:             IrValueId bits = bits_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_load_place_raw(builder, bits_place, bits_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015368:             IrValueId shift = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, width == 32 ? 31u : width == 80 ? 15u : 63u, false, token, bits_type);
015369:             if (bits.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && shift.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015370:             {
015371:                 IrValueId sign = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, bits, shift, bits_type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
015372:                 if (sign.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015373:                 {
015374:                     result = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, sign, builder->s32_type, source);
015375:                 }
015376:             }
015377:         }
015378:     }
015379:     return result;
015380: }

015382: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_math_call(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CToken token, String8 link_name, IrValueId* arguments, u32 argument_count)
015383: {
015384:     // `__builtin_huge_val()` is a constant-valued compiler intrinsic.  Keep
015385:     // it in the math-builtin path so hosted headers can use the spelling
015386:     // without declaring a runtime symbol, but emit the IEEE positive
015387:     // infinity directly in canonical IR.
015388:     if (string_equal(link_name, S8("huge_val")))
015389:     {
015390:         if (argument_count != 0)
015391:         {
015392:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015393:         }
015394:         IrSourceRange source = c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token);
015395:         return c_ir_emit_builtin_float_bits(builder, builder->f64_type, UINT64_C(0x7ff0000000000000), source, S8("HUGE_VAL"));
015396:     }
015397:     // `__builtin_inff()` is the single-precision counterpart used by the
015398:     // hosted <math.h> INFINITY macro.  It is a constant-valued intrinsic, so
015399:     // do not require a runtime `inff` declaration or linker symbol.
015400:     if (string_equal(link_name, S8("inff")))
015401:     {
015402:         if (argument_count != 0)
015403:         {
015404:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015405:         }
015406:         IrSourceRange source = c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token);
015407:         return c_ir_emit_builtin_float_bits(builder, builder->f32_type, UINT64_C(0x7f800000), source, S8("INFF"));
015408:     }
015409:     // The builtin NaN constructors are compile-time values.  Do not create
015410:     // an imported `nan*` symbol: hosted headers use these names before a
015411:     // runtime library declaration exists, and the quiet IEEE payload is
015412:     // target-independent for the f32/f64 types represented by canonical IR.

015416:         {
015417:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015418:         }

015421:         if (!type || type->kind != IR_TYPE_FLOAT)
015422:         {
015423:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015424:         }
015425:         IrSourceRange source = c_ir_token_source_range(builder, token);
015426:         return c_ir_emit_builtin_float_bits(builder, value_type, type->bit_width == 32 ? UINT64_C(0x7fc00000)
015427:                                                                                        : UINT64_C(0x7ff8000000000000),
015428:                                             source, S8("NAN"));

015580:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015581:     }
015582:     IrValueId reference_result = c_ir_add_result(builder, function_type);
015583:     IrSourceRange reference_source = source;

015585:     reference.symbol = symbol;
015586:     reference.result = reference_result;
015587:     IrInstructionId reference_id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, reference, reference_source);
015588:     builder->function->values[reference_result.value].definition = reference_id;
015589:     IrValueId result = c_ir_add_result(builder, value_type);
015590:     IrValueId* operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, argument_count + 1);
015591:     operands[0] = reference_result;

015593:     {

015607: // --- Complex values -------------------------------------------------------
015608: //
015609: // A complex value is an ordinary two-field aggregate by the time it reaches
015610: // the IR (see c_ir_complex_type). Arithmetic uses scalar float opcodes and
015611: // constructs its result with the existing immutable AGGREGATE operation.
015612: // Known constructors expose their scalar operands directly; memory objects
015613: // and non-constructor values retain explicit field loads. Complex lvalues
015614: // keep their object identity. There is no separate complex opcode or cleanup
015615: // pass, and native backends keep the existing aggregate representation.
015616: //
015617: // Which arithmetic each operator gets is Clang's, checked against
015618: // `clang -O0 -S -emit-llvm` for every combination rather than derived:
015619: //   * `+` and `-` are componentwise, and a real operand touches only the real
015620: //     half (the imaginary half of the promoted real operand is a positive
015621: //     zero, and Clang carries the other operand's imaginary part through
015622: //     unchanged rather than adding it).
015623: //   * `*` and `/` with a real operand scale or divide both halves.
015624: //   * `*` and `/` with two complex operands call the compiler runtime --
015625: //     __mulsc3/__muldc3/__multc3 and __divsc3/__divdc3/__divtc3 -- which is
015626: //     what Clang emits without -ffast-math or -fcx-limited-range. Those
015627: //     helpers implement the overflow- and NaN-recovering forms from C11
015628: //     Annex G, and calling them rather than inlining Smith's algorithm is the
015629: //     choice made here: it is bit-for-bit what a Clang-built object does, and
015630: //     the alternative would be a second, subtly different implementation of
===== line 15662 =====

015583:     IrSourceRange reference_source = source;
015584:     IrInstruction reference = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_FUNCTION, function_type);
015585:     reference.symbol = symbol;
015586:     reference.result = reference_result;
015587:     IrInstructionId reference_id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, reference, reference_source);
015588:     builder->function->values[reference_result.value].definition = reference_id;
015589:     IrValueId result = c_ir_add_result(builder, value_type);

015607: // --- Complex values -------------------------------------------------------
015608: //
015609: // A complex value is an ordinary two-field aggregate by the time it reaches
015610: // the IR (see c_ir_complex_type). Arithmetic uses scalar float opcodes and
015611: // constructs its result with the existing immutable AGGREGATE operation.
015612: // Known constructors expose their scalar operands directly; memory objects
015613: // and non-constructor values retain explicit field loads. Complex lvalues
015614: // keep their object identity. There is no separate complex opcode or cleanup
015615: // pass, and native backends keep the existing aggregate representation.
015616: //
015617: // Which arithmetic each operator gets is Clang's, checked against
015618: // `clang -O0 -S -emit-llvm` for every combination rather than derived:
015619: //   * `+` and `-` are componentwise, and a real operand touches only the real
015620: //     half (the imaginary half of the promoted real operand is a positive
015621: //     zero, and Clang carries the other operand's imaginary part through
015622: //     unchanged rather than adding it).
015623: //   * `*` and `/` with a real operand scale or divide both halves.
015624: //   * `*` and `/` with two complex operands call the compiler runtime --
015625: //     __mulsc3/__muldc3/__multc3 and __divsc3/__divdc3/__divtc3 -- which is
015626: //     what Clang emits without -ffast-math or -fcx-limited-range. Those
015627: //     helpers implement the overflow- and NaN-recovering forms from C11
015628: //     Annex G, and calling them rather than inlining Smith's algorithm is the
015629: //     choice made here: it is bit-for-bit what a Clang-built object does, and
015630: //     the alternative would be a second, subtly different implementation of
015631: //     the same numerics living in this file.
015632: //   * `real / complex` also goes to the runtime, with the numerator's
015633: //     imaginary part passed as a positive zero, again matching Clang.
015634: //   * `==` and `!=` compare both halves.
015635: //
015636: // System V x86-64 returns a `long double _Complex` in ST(0)/ST(1) (the psABI's
015637: // COMPLEX_X87 class) where the equivalent struct is returned in memory. That
015638: // is the one place the aggregate model is not the ABI, and it is the only
015639: // thing the backends had to learn about complex: the classifier gives that
015640: // result four X87/X87_UP eightbyte parts, the canonical x86-64 emitter pushes
015641: // the imaginary half and then the real one before its RET and pops them in
015642: // that order after a call, and every other position -- the argument, the
015643: // loads, the stores, the copies -- is the two-field aggregate unchanged.
015644: 
015645: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_float16_negate(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId value, IrTypeId type_id, IrSourceRange source)
015646: {
015647:     IrValueId result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015648:     IrTypeId bits_type = c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_SHORT);
015649:     IrValueId slot = c_ir_emit_temporary(builder, type_id, source);
015650:     if (c_ir_type_is_ieee_binary16(builder, type_id) && bits_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID &&
015651:         slot.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, slot, type_id, value, source))
015652:     {
015653:         IrTypeId bits_pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, bits_type);
015654:         IrValueId address = c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, slot, type_id, source);
015655:         IrValueId bits_address = address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && bits_pointer_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
015656:                                      ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, bits_pointer_type, source)
015657:                                      : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015658:         IrValueId bits_place = bits_address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_dereference_place(builder, bits_address, source)
015659:                                                                               : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015660:         IrValueId bits = bits_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_load_place_raw(builder, bits_place, bits_type, source)
015661:                                                                       : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015662:         IrValueId sign_mask = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x8000), false, (CToken){0}, bits_type);
015663:         IrValueId flipped = bits.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && sign_mask.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
015664:                                 ? c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, bits, sign_mask, bits_type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_XOR, source)
015665:                                 : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015666:         if (flipped.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, bits_place, bits_type, flipped, source))
015667:         {
015668:             result = c_ir_emit_load_place(builder, slot, type_id, source);
015669:         }
015670:     }
015671:     return result;
015672: }

015674: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_unary_value(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId operand, IrTypeId type, IrUnaryOperation operation,
015675:                                                     IrSourceRange source)
015676: {
015677:     IrValueId result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015678:     if (operand.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID &&
015679:         operation == IR_UNARY_FLOAT_NEGATE && c_ir_type_is_ieee_binary16(builder, type))
015680:     {
015681:         result = c_ir_emit_float16_negate(builder, operand, type, source);
015682:     }
015683:     else if (operand.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015684:     {
015685:         result = c_ir_add_result(builder, type);
015686:         IrInstruction instruction = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_UNARY, type);
015687:         instruction.operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 1);
015688:         instruction.operands[0] = operand;
015689:         instruction.operand_count = 1;
015690:         instruction.unary_operation = (u8)operation;
015691:         instruction.result = result;
015692:         IrInstructionId id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, source);
015693:         builder->function->values[result.value].definition = id;
015694:     }
015695:     return result;
015696: }

015698: // GNU's `__real__`/`__imag__` and their unsuffixed spellings, as the unary
015699: // operator each names. The expression walker asks this of every identifier it
015700: // meets where an operand is expected, so the length test carries the common
015701: // answer before any comparison runs.
015702: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_complex_part_operator(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CToken token, CConditionalOperator* operation)
015703: {
015704:     if (token.kind != C_TOKEN_IDENTIFIER)
015705:     {
015706:         return false;
015707:     }
015708:     String8 spelling = c_token_spelling(builder->preprocess.spelling_base, token);
015709:     if (spelling.length != 6 && spelling.length != 8)
015710:     {
015711:         return false;
015712:     }
015713:     if (string_equal(spelling, S8("__real__")) || string_equal(spelling, S8("__real")))
015714:     {
015715:         *operation = C_CONDITIONAL_REAL_PART;
015716:         return true;
015717:     }
015718:     if (string_equal(spelling, S8("__imag__")) || string_equal(spelling, S8("__imag")))
015719:     {
015720:         *operation = C_CONDITIONAL_IMAGINARY_PART;
015721:         return true;
015722:     }
015723:     return false;
015724: }

015741: // The complex type whose halves are `element`, or invalid when `element` is
015742: // not one of the three real floating types a complex type can be built over.
015743: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrTypeId c_ir_complex_type_for_element(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId element)
015744: {
015745:     CTypeKind kind = element.value == builder->f32_type.value            ? C_TYPE_FLOAT_COMPLEX

015897: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_complex_compose(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId complex_type, IrValueId real, IrValueId imaginary,
015898:                                                    IrSourceRange source)
015899: {

015901:     IrType* type = c_ir_complex_type_of(builder, complex_type);
015902:     if (type && real.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && imaginary.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015903:     {
015904:         IrTypeId element = type->element_type;
015905:         real = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, real, element, source);
015906:         imaginary = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, imaginary, element, source);
015907:         if (real.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && imaginary.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015908:         {

015910:             // as a struct initializer. Do not introduce a mutable LOCAL plus
015911:             // two FIELD/STORE pairs and then LOAD it back into a value.
015912:             result = c_ir_add_result(builder, complex_type);

015914:             instruction.operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 2);
015915:             instruction.operands[0] = real;
015916:             instruction.operands[1] = imaginary;
015917:             instruction.operand_count = 2;
015918:             instruction.immediates = arena_allocate(builder->arena, u64, 2);
015919:             instruction.immediates[0] = 0;
015920:             instruction.immediates[1] = 1;
015921:             instruction.immediate_count = 2;
015922:             instruction.result = result;
015923:             IrInstructionId id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, source);
015924:             builder->function->values[result.value].definition = id;
015925:         }
015926:     }
015927:     return result;
015928: }

015930: // Whether a complex value of this type can be computed with here.  Every
015931: // float element this frontend has is admitted; the 80-bit x87 one reaches the
015932: // magnitude below through its sign/exponent halfword rather than through a
015933: // whole-value integer, which is the same view musl's `union ldshape` takes.
015934: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_complex_element_supported(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrType* complex_type)
015935: {
015936:     IrType* element = complex_type ? ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, complex_type->element_type) : 0;
015937:     return element && element->kind == IR_TYPE_FLOAT && (element->bit_width == 32 || element->bit_width == 64 || element->bit_width == 80);
015938: }
015939: 
015940: // |x|, branchless: clear the sign bit through the same stack-slot punning the
015941: // signbit builtin uses, because there is no absolute-value opcode and calling
015942: // libm would make complex division depend on a library.
015943: //
015944: // The 80-bit x87 spelling has no integer of its own width, so it is punned
015945: // one halfword at a time: the sign bit is bit 15 of the sixteen-bit
015946: // sign/exponent field at byte eight, which is exactly the `se` member of
015947: // musl's `union ldshape`, and the ten-byte significand below it is left
015948: // alone.
015949: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_float_magnitude(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId value, IrTypeId type_id, IrSourceRange source)
015950: {
015951:     IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type_id);
015952:     if (!type || type->kind != IR_TYPE_FLOAT || (type->bit_width != 32 && type->bit_width != 64 && type->bit_width != 80))
015953:     {
015954:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015955:     }
015956:     u32 bit_width = type->bit_width;
015957:     CTypeKind bits_kind = bit_width == 32 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT : bit_width == 64 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LONG_LONG : C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_SHORT;
015958:     IrTypeId bits_type = c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, bits_kind);
015959:     IrValueId slot = c_ir_emit_temporary(builder, type_id, source);
015960:     if (bits_type.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || slot.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ||
015961:         !c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, slot, type_id, value, source))
015962:     {
015963:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015964:     }
015965:     IrTypeId bits_pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, bits_type);
015966:     IrValueId address = c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, slot, type_id, source);
015967:     IrValueId bits_address = address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && bits_pointer_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
015968:                                  ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, bits_pointer_type, source)
015969:                                  : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015970:     IrValueId bits_place = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015971:     if (bits_address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015972:     {
015973:         if (bit_width == 80)
015974:         {
015975:             // The fifth halfword of the sixteen-byte slot: byte eight, where
015976:             // the x87 format keeps the sign and the exponent.
015977:             IrValueId halfword_index = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 4, false, (CToken){0}, builder->s32_type);
015978:             bits_place = halfword_index.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_index_place(builder, bits_address, halfword_index, source)
015979:                                                                          : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015980:         }
015981:         else
015982:         {
015983:             bits_place = c_ir_emit_dereference_place(builder, bits_address, source);
015984:         }
015985:     }
015986:     IrValueId bits = bits_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_load_place_raw(builder, bits_place, bits_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015987:     IrValueId mask = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder,
015988:                                                    bit_width == 32   ? UINT64_C(0x7fffffff)
015989:                                                    : bit_width == 64 ? UINT64_C(0x7fffffffffffffff)
015990:                                                                      : UINT64_C(0x7fff),
015991:                                                    false, (CToken){0}, bits_type);
015992:     if (bits.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || mask.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015993:     {
015994:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015995:     }
015996:     IrValueId cleared = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, bits, mask, bits_type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
015997:     if (cleared.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, bits_place, bits_type, cleared, source))
015998:     {
015999:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016000:     }
016001:     return c_ir_emit_load_place(builder, slot, type_id, source);
016002: }
016003: 
016004: // One arm of Smith's algorithm, with `dominant` the denominator half of
016005: // larger magnitude and `lesser` the other one. The obvious names for that pair
016006: // are the two the Windows SDK still defines as empty segment-model macros, so
016007: // a parameter called either of them vanishes and the definition stops being
016008: // one; these two are deliberately not those.
016009: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_emit_complex_smith_arm(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId complex_type, IrTypeId element, IrValueId result_place,
016010:                                                      IrValueId a, IrValueId b, IrValueId dominant, IrValueId lesser, bool dominant_is_real, IrSourceRange source)
016011: {
016012:     IrValueId ratio = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, lesser, dominant, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_DIVIDE, source);
016013:     IrValueId scaled = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, ratio, lesser, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_MULTIPLY, source);
016014:     IrValueId denominator = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, dominant, scaled, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_ADD, source);
016015:     IrValueId real_numerator;
016016:     IrValueId imaginary_numerator;
016017:     if (dominant_is_real)
016018:     {
016019:         // |c| >= |d|: r = d/c, den = c + r*d, (a + b*r)/den and (b - a*r)/den.
016020:         IrValueId b_ratio = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, b, ratio, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_MULTIPLY, source);
016021:         IrValueId a_ratio = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, a, ratio, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_MULTIPLY, source);

016044: // (a + bi) / (c + di) by Smith's algorithm, which is what Clang emits inline
016045: // for `-fcomplex-arithmetic=improved`: divide through by whichever denominator
016046: // half has the larger magnitude so the intermediate `c*c + d*d` of the naive
016047: // form -- which overflows for operands whose squares do not fit -- never
016048: // appears.
016049: //
016050: // Clang's default for C is neither this nor the naive form: it calls
016051: // __divdc3 (and __muldc3 for the product), the compiler-runtime helpers that
016052: // add C11 Annex G's infinity recovery, and for division an ilogb rescaling,
016053: // on top of the same arithmetic. Those helpers live in libgcc or compiler-rt,
016054: // and this toolchain ships neither and links neither, so calling them would
016055: // turn every complex multiply into an unresolved symbol at link time.
016056: //
016057: // The inline forms below were differenced against Clang over an operand
016058: // matrix covering the signed zeroes, the subnormal and overflow edges and the
016059: // infinities. Against `-fcomplex-arithmetic=improved` every answer in that
016060: // matrix is bit-identical, on System V x86-64, AAPCS64 and Win64 alike.
016061: // Against the default they part company in two places, both inside the
016062: // library helpers: Annex G's recovery, where the helper turns a NaN into a
016063: // signed infinity, and a quotient whose operands straddle the format's
016064: // exponent range, where the helper's rescaling rounds one unit in the last
016065: // place differently.

015930: // Whether a complex value of this type can be computed with here.  Every
015931: // float element this frontend has is admitted; the 80-bit x87 one reaches the
015932: // magnitude below through its sign/exponent halfword rather than through a
015933: // whole-value integer, which is the same view musl's `union ldshape` takes.
015934: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_complex_element_supported(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrType* complex_type)
015935: {
015936:     IrType* element = complex_type ? ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, complex_type->element_type) : 0;
015937:     return element && element->kind == IR_TYPE_FLOAT && (element->bit_width == 32 || element->bit_width == 64 || element->bit_width == 80);
015938: }
015939: 
015940: // |x|, branchless: clear the sign bit through the same stack-slot punning the
015941: // signbit builtin uses, because there is no absolute-value opcode and calling
015942: // libm would make complex division depend on a library.
015943: //
015944: // The 80-bit x87 spelling has no integer of its own width, so it is punned
015945: // one halfword at a time: the sign bit is bit 15 of the sixteen-bit
015946: // sign/exponent field at byte eight, which is exactly the `se` member of
015947: // musl's `union ldshape`, and the ten-byte significand below it is left
015948: // alone.
015949: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_float_magnitude(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId value, IrTypeId type_id, IrSourceRange source)
015950: {
015951:     IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type_id);
015952:     if (!type || type->kind != IR_TYPE_FLOAT || (type->bit_width != 32 && type->bit_width != 64 && type->bit_width != 80))
015953:     {
015954:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015955:     }
015956:     u32 bit_width = type->bit_width;
015957:     CTypeKind bits_kind = bit_width == 32 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT : bit_width == 64 ? C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LONG_LONG : C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_SHORT;
015958:     IrTypeId bits_type = c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, bits_kind);
015959:     IrValueId slot = c_ir_emit_temporary(builder, type_id, source);
015960:     if (bits_type.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || slot.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ||
015961:         !c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, slot, type_id, value, source))
015962:     {
015963:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015964:     }
015965:     IrTypeId bits_pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, bits_type);
015966:     IrValueId address = c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, slot, type_id, source);
015967:     IrValueId bits_address = address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && bits_pointer_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
015968:                                  ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, bits_pointer_type, source)
015969:                                  : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015970:     IrValueId bits_place = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015971:     if (bits_address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015972:     {
015973:         if (bit_width == 80)
015974:         {
015975:             // The fifth halfword of the sixteen-byte slot: byte eight, where
015976:             // the x87 format keeps the sign and the exponent.
015977:             IrValueId halfword_index = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 4, false, (CToken){0}, builder->s32_type);
015978:             bits_place = halfword_index.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_index_place(builder, bits_address, halfword_index, source)
015979:                                                                          : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015980:         }
015981:         else
015982:         {
015983:             bits_place = c_ir_emit_dereference_place(builder, bits_address, source);
015984:         }
015985:     }
015986:     IrValueId bits = bits_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_load_place_raw(builder, bits_place, bits_type, source) : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015987:     IrValueId mask = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder,
015988:                                                    bit_width == 32   ? UINT64_C(0x7fffffff)
015989:                                                    : bit_width == 64 ? UINT64_C(0x7fffffffffffffff)
015990:                                                                      : UINT64_C(0x7fff),
015991:                                                    false, (CToken){0}, bits_type);
015992:     if (bits.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || mask.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015993:     {
015994:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015995:     }
015996:     IrValueId cleared = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, bits, mask, bits_type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
015997:     if (cleared.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, bits_place, bits_type, cleared, source))
015998:     {
015999:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016000:     }
016001:     return c_ir_emit_load_place(builder, slot, type_id, source);
016002: }

016004: // One arm of Smith's algorithm, with `dominant` the denominator half of
016005: // larger magnitude and `lesser` the other one. The obvious names for that pair
016006: // are the two the Windows SDK still defines as empty segment-model macros, so
016007: // a parameter called either of them vanishes and the definition stops being
016008: // one; these two are deliberately not those.
016009: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_emit_complex_smith_arm(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId complex_type, IrTypeId element, IrValueId result_place,
016010:                                                      IrValueId a, IrValueId b, IrValueId dominant, IrValueId lesser, bool dominant_is_real, IrSourceRange source)
016011: {
016012:     IrValueId ratio = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, lesser, dominant, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_DIVIDE, source);
016013:     IrValueId scaled = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, ratio, lesser, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_MULTIPLY, source);
016014:     IrValueId denominator = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, dominant, scaled, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_ADD, source);
016015:     IrValueId real_numerator;
016016:     IrValueId imaginary_numerator;
016017:     if (dominant_is_real)
016018:     {
016019:         // |c| >= |d|: r = d/c, den = c + r*d, (a + b*r)/den and (b - a*r)/den.
016020:         IrValueId b_ratio = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, b, ratio, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_MULTIPLY, source);
016021:         IrValueId a_ratio = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, a, ratio, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_MULTIPLY, source);
016022:         real_numerator = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, a, b_ratio, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_ADD, source);
016023:         imaginary_numerator = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, b, a_ratio, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_SUBTRACT, source);
016024:     }
016025:     else
016026:     {
016027:         // |d| > |c|: r = c/d, den = d + r*c, (a*r + b)/den and (b*r - a)/den.
016028:         IrValueId a_ratio = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, a, ratio, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_MULTIPLY, source);
016029:         IrValueId b_ratio = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, b, ratio, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_MULTIPLY, source);
016030:         real_numerator = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, a_ratio, b, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_ADD, source);
016031:         imaginary_numerator = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, b_ratio, a, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_SUBTRACT, source);
016032:     }
016033:     IrValueId real = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, real_numerator, denominator, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_DIVIDE, source);
016034:     IrValueId imaginary = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, imaginary_numerator, denominator, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_DIVIDE, source);
016035:     IrValueId real_place = c_ir_emit_field_index_place(builder, result_place, 0, source);
016036:     IrValueId imaginary_place = c_ir_emit_field_index_place(builder, result_place, 1, source);
016037:     BUSTER_UNUSED(complex_type);
016038:     return real.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && imaginary.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID &&
016039:            real_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && imaginary_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID &&
016040:            c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, real_place, element, real, source) &&
016041:            c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, imaginary_place, element, imaginary, source);
016042: }

016112: // halves convert independently, a real value gains a positive-zero imaginary
016113: // part, and a complex value converted to a real type keeps its real half.

016115: {

016123:         {
016124:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016125:         }

016127:         {
016128:             return c_ir_emit_cast(builder, real, target_type, source);
016129:         }

016132:         imaginary = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, imaginary, target_element, source);

016162: // `__real__ E` and `__imag__ E` as values. GNU allows either on a real
016163: // operand too: `__real__ x` is `x` and `__imag__ x` is a positive zero of
016164: // x's type, which is what Clang emits, and it is what makes the operators
016165: // usable in code that is generic over real and complex.
016166: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_complex_part_operator(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId value, bool imaginary, IrSourceRange source)
016167: {

016169:     if (!complex_type)

016172:         {

016178:         {
016179:             builder->failure_message = S8("__real__ and __imag__ require an arithmetic operand");
016180:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016181:         }
016182:         if (!imaginary)
016183:         {
016184:             return value;
016185:         }
016186:         return type->kind == IR_TYPE_FLOAT ? c_ir_complex_zero(builder, type_id, source)
016187:                                            : c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 0, false, (CToken){0}, type_id);
016188:     }
016189:     IrTypeId element = complex_type->element_type;
016190:     IrValueId place = c_ir_complex_operand_place(builder, value, source);
016191:     if (place.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
016192:     {
016193:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016194:     }
016195:     return c_ir_complex_part(builder, place, element, imaginary ? 1u : 0u, source);
016196: }

016198: // `+ - * /`, unary `-`, GNU unary `~` (conjugation) and `== !=` where at
016199: // least one operand is complex. Everything else -- the remaining bitwise and
016200: // the relational operators, `%` -- has no complex form in C and is refused
016201: // here rather than silently applied to the real half.
016202: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_apply_complex_operation(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CConditionalOperator operation, IrValueId* values, u32* value_count,
016203:                                                       u32 first, u32 operand_count, IrSourceRange source)
016204: {
016205:     IrTypeId left_type = builder->function->values[values[first].value].canonical_type;
016206:     IrTypeId right_type = operand_count == 2 ? builder->function->values[values[first + 1].value].canonical_type : left_type;
016207:     IrTypeId result_type = c_ir_complex_result_type(builder, left_type, right_type);
016208:     IrType* result_complex = c_ir_complex_type_of(builder, result_type);
016209:     if (!result_complex)
016210:     {
016211:         builder->failure_message = S8("unsupported complex operand type");
016212:         return false;
016213:     }
016214:     IrTypeId element = result_complex->element_type;
016215:     bool left_complex = c_ir_complex_type_of(builder, left_type) != 0;
016216:     bool right_complex = operand_count == 2 && c_ir_complex_type_of(builder, right_type) != 0;
016217:     IrValueId real = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016218:     IrValueId imaginary = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016219:     if (operand_count == 1)
016220:     {
016221:         // GNU spells complex conjugation `~` -- C99 Annex G's `conj` -- so the
016222:         // one bitwise operator that has no complex form on a real operand does
016223:         // have one here. It negates the imaginary half alone; unary `-`
016224:         // negates both.
016225:         if (operation != C_CONDITIONAL_UNARY_MINUS && operation != C_CONDITIONAL_BITWISE_NOT)
016226:         {
016227:             builder->failure_message = S8("this unary operator has no complex form");
016228:             return false;
016229:         }
016230:         IrValueId converted = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[first], result_type, source);
016231:         if (converted.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !c_ir_complex_split(builder, converted, &real, &imaginary, source))
016232:         {
016233:             return false;
016234:         }
016235:         real = operation == C_CONDITIONAL_UNARY_MINUS ? c_ir_emit_unary_value(builder, real, element, IR_UNARY_FLOAT_NEGATE, source) : real;
016236:         imaginary = c_ir_emit_unary_value(builder, imaginary, element, IR_UNARY_FLOAT_NEGATE, source);
016237:         IrValueId negated = c_ir_complex_compose(builder, result_type, real, imaginary, source);
016238:         if (negated.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
016239:         {
016240:             return false;
016241:         }
016242:         *value_count = first;
016243:         values[(*value_count)++] = negated;
016244:         return true;
016245:     }
016246:     // Both operands are read before anything is emitted for the operation, so
016247:     // the two splits below cannot interleave with each other's field loads.
016248:     IrValueId left_real = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016249:     IrValueId left_imaginary = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016250:     IrValueId right_real = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016251:     IrValueId right_imaginary = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016252:     if (left_complex)
016253:     {
016254:         IrValueId converted = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[first], result_type, source);
016255:         if (converted.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !c_ir_complex_split(builder, converted, &left_real, &left_imaginary, source))
016256:         {
016257:             return false;
016258:         }
016259:     }
016260:     else
016261:     {
016262:         left_real = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[first], element, source);
016263:     }
016264:     if (right_complex)
016265:     {
016266:         IrValueId converted = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[first + 1], result_type, source);
016267:         if (converted.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !c_ir_complex_split(builder, converted, &right_real, &right_imaginary, source))
016268:         {
016269:             return false;
016270:         }
016271:     }
016272:     else
016273:     {
016274:         right_real = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[first + 1], element, source);
016275:     }
016276:     if (left_real.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || right_real.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
016277:     {
016278:         return false;
016279:     }
016280:     IrValueId result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016281:     switch (operation)
016282:     {
016283:     case C_CONDITIONAL_ADD:
016284:     {
016285:         real = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, left_real, right_real, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_ADD, source);
016286:         imaginary = left_complex && right_complex
016287:                         ? c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, left_imaginary, right_imaginary, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_ADD, source)
016288:                         : (left_complex ? left_imaginary : right_imaginary);
016289:         result = c_ir_complex_compose(builder, result_type, real, imaginary, source);
016290:         break;
016291:     }
016292:     case C_CONDITIONAL_SUBTRACT:
016293:     {
016294:         real = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, left_real, right_real, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_SUBTRACT, source);
016295:         if (left_complex && right_complex)
016296:         {
016297:             imaginary = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, left_imaginary, right_imaginary, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_SUBTRACT, source);
016298:         }
016299:         else if (left_complex)
016300:         {
016301:             imaginary = left_imaginary;
016302:         }
016303:         else
016304:         {
016305:             imaginary = c_ir_emit_unary_value(builder, right_imaginary, element, IR_UNARY_FLOAT_NEGATE, source);
016306:         }
016307:         result = c_ir_complex_compose(builder, result_type, real, imaginary, source);
===== line 18190 =====
018110:     }
018111:     u32 remaining = builder->prepared_call_count - first_new;

018113:     struct CIrCallEmissionTask
018114:     {
018115:         u32 call_index;
018116:         bool finish;
018117:         u8 reserved[3];
018118:     };

018120:     u32* emission_order = arena_allocate(builder->temporary_arena, u32, remaining ? remaining : 1);
018121:     u32 task_count = 0;
018122:     u32 emission_count = 0;
018123:     for (u32 root = last_root; root != UINT32_MAX; root = builder->prepared_calls[root].previous_sibling_index)
018124:     {

018126:             .call_index = root,
018127:         };
018128:     }

018130:     {
018131:         CIrCallEmissionTask task = tasks[--task_count];
018132:         CIrPreparedCall* call = builder->prepared_calls + task.call_index;
018133:         if (task.finish)
018134:         {
018135:             emission_order[emission_count++] = task.call_index;
018136:             continue;
018137:         }
018138:         tasks[task_count++] = (CIrCallEmissionTask){
018139:             .call_index = task.call_index,
018140:             .finish = true,
018141:         };
018142:         for (u32 child = call->last_child_index; child != UINT32_MAX; child = builder->prepared_calls[child].previous_sibling_index)
018143:         {
018144:             tasks[task_count++] = (CIrCallEmissionTask){
018145:                 .call_index = child,
018146:             };
018147:         }
018148:     }
018149:     BUSTER_CHECK(emission_count == remaining);
018150:     *emission_order_out = emission_order;
018151:     *emission_count_out = emission_count;
018152:     return true;
018153: }

018155: // The one vector type the 512-bit vocabulary speaks in: 64 bytes of u8. Every
018156: // builtin that returns a vector returns this, and `Simd512` in
018157: // <buster/lib/simd.h> is declared to match, so no conversion ever appears at a
018158: // call site. The layout matches what the `vector_size` attribute produces for
018159: // the same spelling, so the two are the same IR type and not two that happen to
018160: // agree.
018161: // __builtin_popcount is one instruction where the target has POPCNT and the
018162: // classic SWAR sequence where it does not, decided here rather than in the
018163: // backends: an IR expansion is the same handful of ordinary instructions every
018164: // backend already emits, and it keeps AArch64 from needing a NEON round trip
018165: // for a scalar operation the compiler itself barely uses.
018166: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_population_count(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId operand, IrTypeId type, CToken token, IrSourceRange source)
018167: {
018168:     IrType* integer = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type);
018169:     if (!integer || integer->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER)
018170:     {
018171:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018172:     }
018173:     if (target_cpu_feature_has(builder->target, TARGET_CPU_FEATURE_X86_POPCNT))
018174:     {
018175:         IrValueId result = c_ir_add_result(builder, type);
018176:         IrInstruction instruction = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_UNARY, type);
018177:         instruction.operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 1);
018178:         instruction.operands[0] = operand;
018179:         instruction.operand_count = 1;
018180:         instruction.unary_operation = IR_UNARY_INTEGER_POPULATION_COUNT;
018181:         instruction.result = result;
018182:         builder->function->values[result.value].definition = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, source);
018183:         return result;
018184:     }
018185:     // The classic SWAR sequence: subtract the odd bits to make two-bit sums,
018186:     // add the pairs into four-bit sums, fold to bytes, then let one multiply
018187:     // gather every byte sum into the top byte.
018188:     u32 width = integer->bit_width;
018189:     u64 mask = width >= 64 ? UINT64_MAX : (((u64)1 << width) - 1);
018190:     IrValueId one = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 1, false, token, type);
018191:     IrValueId odd_bits = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x5555555555555555) & mask, false, token, type);
018192:     IrValueId shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, operand, one, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018193:     IrValueId high = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, shifted, odd_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018194:     IrValueId value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, operand, high, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_SUBTRACT, source);
018195:     IrValueId two = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 2, false, token, type);
018196:     IrValueId pair_bits = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x3333333333333333) & mask, false, token, type);
018197:     shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, two, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018198:     high = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, shifted, pair_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018199:     IrValueId low = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, pair_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018200:     value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, low, high, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_ADD, source);
018201:     IrValueId four = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 4, false, token, type);
018202:     IrValueId nibble_mask = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x0f0f0f0f0f0f0f0f) & mask, false, token, type);
018203:     shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, four, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018204:     IrValueId summed = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, shifted, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_ADD, source);
018205:     value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, summed, nibble_mask, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018206:     IrValueId ones = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x0101010101010101) & mask, false, token, type);
018207:     IrValueId gathered = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, ones, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_MULTIPLY, source);
018208:     IrValueId top = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, width - 8, false, token, type);
018209:     return c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, gathered, top, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018210: }

018212: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrTypeId c_ir_simd_vector_type(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder)
018213: {
018214:     IrTypeId element = builder->scalar_types[C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_CHAR];
018215:     IrType* element_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, element);
018216:     if (!element_type || element_type->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER || element_type->bit_width != 8)
018217:     {
018218:         return IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
018219:     }
018220:     for (u32 type_index = 0; type_index < builder->program->types.count; type_index += 1)
018221:     {
018222:         IrType* candidate = builder->program->types.types + type_index;
018223:         if (candidate->kind == IR_TYPE_VECTOR && candidate->element_type.value == element.value && candidate->element_count == 64 &&
018224:             candidate->layout.size == 64)
018225:         {
018226:             return candidate->id;
018227:         }
018228:     }
018229:     return ir_program_add_type(builder->program, (IrType){
018230:                                                      .name = S8("GNU vector"),
018231:                                                      .element_type = element,
018232:                                                      .return_type = IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID,
018233:                                                      .layout =
018234:                                                          {
018235:                                                              .size = 64,
018236:                                                              .alignment = 64,
018237:                                                              .resolved = true,
018238:                                                          },
018239:                                                      .kind = IR_TYPE_VECTOR,
018240:                                                      .element_count = 64,
018241:                                                      .bit_width = 512,
018242:                                                  });
018243: }

018245: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrTypeId c_ir_simd_result_type(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrSimdOperation operation)
018246: {

018257: // Arguments get exactly the conversions C would already have applied at a call
018258: // with this prototype: arrays decay, integers convert. A vector argument is
018259: // checked and never converted — a silent lane reinterpretation is the one
018260: // thing an explicit SIMD kernel must not get.
018261: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_simd_coerce_argument(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId value, CIrSimdArgument kind, IrSourceRange source)
018262: {
018263:     if (value.value < builder->function->value_count)
018264:     {
018265:         IrTypeId type_id = builder->function->values[value.value].canonical_type;
018266:         IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type_id);
018267:         if (type)
018268:         {
018269:             switch (kind)
018270:             {
018271:             case C_IR_SIMD_ARGUMENT_ADDRESS:
018272:             {
018273:                 if (type->kind == IR_TYPE_ARRAY || type->kind == IR_TYPE_VECTOR)
018274:                 {
018275:                     IrTypeId pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, type->element_type);
018276:                     value = c_ir_decay_array(builder, value, pointer_type, source);
018277:                     type = value.value < builder->function->value_count ? ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, builder->function->values[value.value].canonical_type) : 0;
018278:                 }
018279:                 return type && type->kind == IR_TYPE_POINTER ? value : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018280:             }
018281:             case C_IR_SIMD_ARGUMENT_MASK:
018282:                 return type->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER || type->kind == IR_TYPE_BOOLEAN || type->kind == IR_TYPE_ENUM
018283:                            ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, value, builder->scalar_types[C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LONG_LONG], source)
018284:                            : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018285:             case C_IR_SIMD_ARGUMENT_BYTE:
018286:                 return type->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER || type->kind == IR_TYPE_BOOLEAN || type->kind == IR_TYPE_ENUM
018287:                            ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, value, builder->scalar_types[C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_CHAR], source)
018288:                            : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018289:             case C_IR_SIMD_ARGUMENT_WORD:
018290:                 return type->kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER || type->kind == IR_TYPE_BOOLEAN || type->kind == IR_TYPE_ENUM
018291:                            ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, value, builder->scalar_types[C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT], source)
018292:                            : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018293:             case C_IR_SIMD_ARGUMENT_VECTOR:
018294:                 return type->kind == IR_TYPE_VECTOR && type->layout.resolved && type->layout.size == 64 ? value : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018295:             case C_IR_SIMD_ARGUMENT_IMMEDIATE:
018296:                 break;
018297:             }
018298:         }
018299:     }
018300: 
018301:     return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
018302: }

018196:     IrValueId pair_bits = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x3333333333333333) & mask, false, token, type);
018197:     shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, two, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018198:     high = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, shifted, pair_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018199:     IrValueId low = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, pair_bits, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018200:     value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, low, high, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_ADD, source);
018201:     IrValueId four = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 4, false, token, type);
018202:     IrValueId nibble_mask = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x0f0f0f0f0f0f0f0f) & mask, false, token, type);
018203:     shifted = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, four, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018204:     IrValueId summed = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, shifted, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_ADD, source);
018205:     value = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, summed, nibble_mask, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_AND, source);
018206:     IrValueId ones = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x0101010101010101) & mask, false, token, type);
018207:     IrValueId gathered = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, value, ones, type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_MULTIPLY, source);
018208:     IrValueId top = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, width - 8, false, token, type);
018209:     return c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, gathered, top, type, IR_BINARY_UNSIGNED_SHIFT_RIGHT, source);
018210: }
